task05_x_nbni3.hint: Nb atoms per formula divided by all atoms per formula; one sublattice holds the Nb.

task05_x_nb7ni6.hint: Seven of the thirteen sites per formula hold Nb; use x_nb with whole sublattices filled.

task05_atoms_delta.hint: Add the sites per formula of all δ sublattices.

task05_atoms_mu.hint: Add the sites per formula of all μ sublattices.

task05_delta_hand_1000.hint: Use the function's branch whose range contains 1000 K, then apply the endmember's own multiplier and added constant. The result is per mole of formula units.

task05_delta_atom.hint: Divide the formula energy once by the atoms per δ formula.

task05_mu_atom.hint: Divide the formula energy once by the atoms per μ formula.

task05_divide_gm_again.hint: GM is already per mole of atoms. Answer True or False.

task05_amount_sum.hint: Add the two NP values as given.

task05_nb_balance.hint: Multiply each phase's NP by its x(Nb) and add; do not divide NP by the atoms per formula.

task05_ni_balance.hint: Multiply each phase's NP by its 1 − x(Nb) and add.

task05_delta_formula_units.hint: δ's NP divided by the atoms per δ formula.

task05_mu_formula_units.hint: μ's NP divided by the atoms per μ formula.

task05_formula_weights_balance.hint: Try it: normalise the two formula-unit amounts, weight the x(Nb) values and compare. Answer True or False.

task05_eut040_liquid.hint: Run column(0.40): the lowest temperature at which the cell is LIQUID alone.

task05_eut040_solid.hint: Run column(0.40): the highest temperature at which the cell has no LIQUID.

task05_eut016_liquid.hint: Run column(0.16): the lowest temperature at which the cell is LIQUID alone.

task05_eut016_solid.hint: Run column(0.16): the highest temperature at which the cell has no LIQUID.

task05_eut016_nb_richer.hint: Of the two solids just below the liquid, take the one with the larger x(Nb) in the phase; type its name as in the table.

task05_mu_atoms_per_cell.hint: The block holds 2 × 2 × 1 = 4 cells: divide its total by 4.

task05_mu_formula_per_cell.hint: Atoms per cell divided by 13 atoms per μ formula.

task05_mu_18h_per_formula.hint: 18h atoms in one cell divided by the formula units per cell.

task05_mu_6c_order_known.hint: The database numbers sublattices but names no crystal sites. Answer True or False.
